text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: 3.2x increase in 5xxs for customer 'oxbow-fin' on dedicated-vpc-us-west-2 (pool: oxbow-pool-01). P50 latency +1.4x, P99 +3.8x. Incident severity: P2. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/oxbow-vpc-fallback
Maya K: paging oncall now - I'm on it. reading metrics.
oncall-rot: acked. grabbing pager.
Sam R: I see spike in evictions and model swap chatter in logs - `model-manager`: evicting model oxbow-prod-v3 -> fallback to cpu-quantized-v1. evict reason: memory pressure.
Elena P: @Sam R can you post the exact log lines? need to confirm if it's eviction storm or a single host OOM.
Sam R: paste: ```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z model-manager INFO evict model=oxbow-prod-v3 host=gpu-17 reason=kv-cache-pressure mem_free=1.2GB
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z runtime WARN fallback to=cpu-quantized-v1 request_id=abc123 latency=1200ms
```
Maya K: this matches user reports from Oxbow support - they see slowness and failing requests. Jordan (CSM): are they on Dedicated?
Jordan (CSM): yes, oxbow-fin is on a Dedicated VPC with reserved pool oxbow-pool-01. They're already on a higher SLA plan. They're on-call on their side too, pinging their infra.
Anu I: quick analysis: pool utilization spike (90->99%) at 09:11, multiple model versions loaded concurrently. Looks like a churn where a canary rollout triggered new weights then evictions. I think safe move is pin customer routing to oxbow-prod-v2 (previous stable) or to our safe-variant `oxbow-stable-lite` while we stabilize.
Maya K: agree. we should do a tenant-level override to route oxbow-fin to `oxbow-stable-lite` (safe variant) with an autoscale increase if possible. Any objections?
Sam R: no objections. prefer variant over scale up to avoid immediate cost/contention. Also need to ensure `oxbow-stable-lite` has same tokenization/schema for tool calls.
Elena P: confirmed: `oxbow-stable-lite` is compatible. small diffs in response length but safe.
Maya K: Jordan, can we tell customer we'll route them to a safe variant for the next 30 mins while we fix underlying eviction?
Jordan (CSM): yes, they want fast mitigation. message ready: "Routing you to a stable variant to restore throughput; no prompts/data will be changed." I'll send once we confirm override.
Maya K: executing override now. command: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/overrides 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"tenant":"oxbow-fin","route":"model","target":"oxbow-stable-lite","duration":1800,"reason":"eviction storm - emergency safe variant"}'
```
deploy-bot: override created id=ovr-20260315-889 status=active target=oxbow-stable-lite scope=tenant:oxbow-fin
oncall-rot: started smoke checks against oxbow-fin routing. hitting /health and a sample workload.
Sam R: I'm watching infra. also bumping pool autoscale target by +1 GPU as precaution (if the override doesn't lower load). command run: ```bash
rdctl pools update --pool oxbow-pool-01 --min-gpus 2 --max-gpus 6 --comment "temp bump during oxbow incident"
```
Anu I: adding notes: we should also pin their model version in routing so the platform doesn't try canary swaps mid-incident. I'll create a pin for `oxbow-prod-v2` in case we need to rollback to a previous exact model.
Maya K: create both: tenant override to stable-lite, and a pinned model record for oxbow-fin -> oxbow-prod-v2 (safe rollback). Command snippet: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/pins 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' 
 -d '{"tenant":"oxbow-fin","model":"oxbow-prod-v2","expires_in":3600,"reason":"emergency pin during rollback"}'
```
deploy-bot: pin created id=pin-991 status=active model=oxbow-prod-v2 tenant=oxbow-fin expires_at=2026-03-15T10:18:22Z
Jordan (CSM): messaging customer now. sending: "We've routed you to a stable variant and pinned your tenant to a previously verified model. This should restore normal throughput in ~1-2 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."
Maya K: smoke checks green. p99 for oxbow-fin dropped from 4.2s -> 320ms. 5xxs nearly zero.
Sam R: logs show fallbacks stopped. eviction rate back to baseline. I'll keep watch for 15m.
Anu I: follow-up actions: 1) investigate canary rollout that caused memory pressure (owner: eng-ml/canary team) 2) evaluate KV cache sizing and eviction thresholds for dedicated pools (owner: eng-runtime) 3) postmortem with customer-facing summary (owner: Maya K + Jordan).
Elena P: adding playbook checklist to the incident runbook: tenant override, pin, autoscale bump, and customer comms.
Maya K: assigning pager for morning shift to run a root cause once ML team posts findings. @oncall-rot you're up for 6am handoff if still open.
oncall-rot: will follow up, noted.
Jordan (CSM): customer acked and appreciates the quick mitigation. asked for ETA on RCA by EOD. I'll coordinate.
Maya K: changing incident status -> stabilized. creating incident ticket INC-oxbow-20260315 and adding timeline + commands used.
incident-bot: Incident INC-oxbow-20260315 created. severity=P2 state=stabilized owner=Maya K runbook=oxbow-vpc-fallback
Maya K: thanks all. small note: we'll leave override active for 30m then re-evaluate before removing pin. please don't run new canaries in oxbow pool until RCA closed. :pray:
Sam R: adding to canary dashboard watchlist.
Elena P: postmortem owner confirmed. Jordan, I'll draft the technical appendix.
Jordan (CSM): I'll draft customer-facing summary.
Maya K: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
